items.followUp: What is a router, and what does it do in a network?

rubric.why: Award one mark for identifying a switch as a network device that connects computers or other devices.
rubric.description: Identifies a switch as a device that connects computers or other devices.
rubric.how: Look for the idea that it is a device and connects computers or devices.

rubric.why: Award one mark for explaining that a switch forwards data to its intended device.
rubric.description: Explains that the switch forwards data to the intended device.
rubric.how: Look for forwarding data and identifying its intended device or destination.

modelAnswer: A switch is a network device that connects computers and other devices in a local area network (LAN).
It forwards data to the intended device on the network.

items.followUp: What is an algorithm, and how can pseudocode help before programming?

rubric.why: Award one mark for stating that pseudocode expresses or represents the steps of an algorithm.
rubric.description: Explains that pseudocode represents an algorithm's steps.
rubric.how: Look for pseudocode, an algorithm, and its steps.

rubric.why: Award one mark for explaining that pseudocode helps plan a solution before writing code.
rubric.description: Explains its use in planning a solution before coding.
rubric.how: Look for planning and the idea that this happens before coding.

modelAnswer: Pseudocode expresses the steps of an algorithm in simple, human-readable language.
It helps plan and check the logic of a solution before writing program code.

items.followUp: What is the purpose of the <title> tag in an HTML document?

rubric.why: Award one mark for stating that the head contains information or metadata about the HTML document.
rubric.description: States that the head contains document information or metadata.
rubric.how: Look for the head section and information or metadata about the document.

rubric.why: Award one mark for naming valid content that can be placed in the head, such as the page title, a stylesheet link, or a script reference.
rubric.description: Gives a valid example of content placed inside the head.
rubric.how: Look for the title, stylesheet link, or script reference.

modelAnswer: The <head> tag contains information (metadata) about an HTML document that is not displayed as the page's main content.
It can contain the page title, links to stylesheets, and references to scripts.

items.followUp: What does HTML do in a web page?

rubric.why: Award one mark for expanding CSS as Cascading Style Sheets.
rubric.description: Gives the full form of CSS.
rubric.how: Look for the words Cascading, Style, and Sheets.

rubric.why: Award one mark for explaining that CSS controls the appearance or presentation of web pages.
rubric.description: Explains that CSS controls the appearance of web pages.
rubric.how: Look for controlling appearance or presentation on the web.

modelAnswer: CSS stands for Cascading Style Sheets.
It is a stylesheet language used to control the appearance, formatting, and layout of web pages.
